gen-dafont-pixel-operator-fs-public-sans: Retro and unapologetically digital, Pixel Operator sets its fixed-width letters like terminal blocks. Public Sans does the opposite job, with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters that make ordinary sentences easy to settle into.
gen-dafont-pixel-operator-inter: Pixel Operator spaces every letter into the same fixed-width cell, so words land like solid blocks. And Inter, a plain sans with smooth, tube-like lines and big counters in a tall lowercase, flows in the opposite way.
gen-dafont-pixel-operator-satoshi: Chunky, blocky, unmistakably terminal: Pixel Operator hammers out fixed-width letters with a retro glow. Satoshi's ribbon-like strokes feel friendlier beside it.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-bespoke-sans: Plakkaat hits hard, its heavy display letters curling round until the terminals nearly touch the stem. But Bespoke Sans stays sharp and refined, leaving generous space where its curves end, so a longer passage reads with ease.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-chillax: Heavy and loud, Plakkaat closes its letters tight like bent straw. Chillax, with its spaghetti-loose lines and unfinished loops, is the relaxed counterweight that makes the pair so lively.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-erode: Plakkaat's lines have zero thick and thin variation, like bent straw. Erode, a classic serif with a tall middle band and gentle ebb in its stroke, gives that bold heading a dignified partner, and it looks best at a modest size.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-ranade: Ranade feels organic and professional, its weight shifting only slightly. Plakkaat's closed, heavy letters make a firm contrast, and the plain sans text can stay at a modest size while its wide-set strokes breathe.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-domine: Domine brings a refined text serif, with compact ascenders and a faint nib-pressure swell in each round letter. And Plakkaat, wire-bent and heavy across the whole word, gives the page a loud opening before that quieter texture takes over.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-graduate: Plakkaat's terminals sweep around until they nearly touch the stem. Graduate, a dignified serif with generous white between letters, leaves open room beneath that heavy, closed heading, so the two settle into clear roles.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu reads in a professional, open way, with wide-open s curves and tiny gaps above the x-height. Plakkaat's heavy closed letters sit above it like a plain stripe of ink, and a longer passage moves along smoothly beneath.
